correctness.rationale: The matrix entries are the Haar-basis matrix coefficients of the positive Carleman operator after reflection. Hence every finite matrix is a compression and has norm at most \(\pi\). The union of the finite Haar spaces is dense in the mean-zero subspace of \(L^2(0,1)\). A compactly supported Carleman near-extremizer can be dilated into \((0,1/2)\), corrected by a term of norm \(O(a^{1/2})\) supported in \([1/2,1]\) to enforce zero mean, normalized, and then approximated by a finite Haar sum. Its Rayleigh quotient stays arbitrarily close to \(\pi\), proving the directed lower limit and therefore the stated limit. No finite numerical extrapolation is needed.
